ensemble_handling: Representative member sheet: the Ace of Clubs soldier. All ten are identical in cut, colour and cap; only pip count/index and natural faces differ (variation_rules), so one member defines the uniform. The Ace was chosen because it is the only club rank not also claimed by a gardener (see DEF-p4-char-301).

sheets.prompt:
Four-panel character reference sheet following the reference layout: three full-body views (front / side / back) left to right, and one large head-and-shoulders close-up filling the right column; the exact same character, outfit and proportions in every panel; plain background. The first reference image is only the panel layout guide: copy its four-panel arrangement, not its grey mannequin shapes. Panel 1 (left): full-body front view, standing at attention, showing the card face of the tabard. Panel 2: full-body true side profile, showing how thin and flat the card tabard is. Panel 3: full-body back view showing the card-back pattern of the tabard. Panel 4 (tall right column): head-and-shoulders close-up, facing the camera, neutral expression, face clearly lit under the cap. Each full-body figure is drawn a little small inside its panel, complete from the top of the cap to the soles of the boots with clear space above and below, standing on a small patch of plain floor with a soft contact shadow; if any part is cut off by the panel edge the sheet is wrong. Plain soft grey-green studio backdrop in every panel, even soft daylight, no scenery, no captions or labels.

Subject: ONE soldier of the Queen of Hearts' guard, alone on the sheet: a young man about 27 years old, a real human actor. Lean, flexible, matched build, about 179 cm tall. Short regulation military crop of brown hair and a neat brown moustache; grey eyes; stolid, drilled, expressionless face. He reads oblong and flat like a playing card: the rigid card tabard makes a flat rectangle of his body, with his arms and legs emerging at its four corners. His uniform follows the group rule, quoted verbatim from the costume bible: '1862 soldiers dressed as living playing cards of the club suit: stiff flat oblong ivory card tabards hanging front and back to the knee, the fronts with black club pips and matching corner rank indices, the backs in a crimson-and-cream lattice card-back pattern with a small heart rosette, over crimson wool shell-jacket sleeves with brass cuff buttons, crimson trousers with a narrow black side stripe, black ankle boots and small black pillbox caps with a brass club badge; rigid, matched and identical'. On this one soldier that means he is the Ace of Clubs: the ivory card front carries a single large black club pip in the centre and a small 'A' index with a small club in the top-left and bottom-right corners. He carries a short ceremonial black-painted wooden baton topped with a three-lobed club-pip finial, held upright at his shoulder.

Style: Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.

Layout recap (highest priority): four separate panels side by side, exactly one soldier in each panel, the same man in front / side / back full-body views and one head-and-shoulders close-up.
